subject: beetle
reasoning:
I'm planning to build a stag beetle model with the agentic-3js-builder SDK, thinking through realistic scale—roughly 5-7cm total length including the male's prominent mandibles, scaled appropriately in meters for the scene.

I'm sketching the design: glossy dark elytra, reddish-brown head, large branched mandibles like antlers, six jointed legs, clubbed antennae, compound eyes, and a pronotum shield. I'm working out the skeleton structure—placing the body joint, then head, mandible, antenna, and leg joints relative to it, trying to keep the hierarchy simple while using the SDK's joint and limb functions correctly to avoid errors.

Now I'm figuring out leg placement for all six legs, naming each chain segment (hip, knee, ankle, foot) and setting their lengths so feet touch the floor, then roughing out where the head and mandibles sit relative to the body coordinates.

For the elytra I'm considering using scaled sphere geometry to form ellipsoid shells rather than modeling complex curves, keeping with the blocky, faceted low-poly aesthetic — splitting them into left and right halves with a visible seam down the back.

Now I'm designing the mandibles as curved chains sweeping forward and inward with tapered radius, adding inner tooth spikes branching off partway along each mandible using the spike primitive anchored to a point on the chain path.

For antennae I'll build elbowed chains from the head with a flattened lamellae club at each tip made from a few stacked spheres, and for legs I'm placing hip joints along the thorax sides at varying heights for front/middle/hind pairs, using three-segment limbs with bend directions to make the knees articulate correctly in their natural plane.

Now I'm computing the foot target distances to confirm each leg's reach is sufficient, then setting up named sweep chains per leg with tapered radii for a tarsus-like leg shape, and planning the dark brown/black color scheme with reddish-brown accents on the mandibles and head, possibly using a grain texture paint on the elytra.

I'm positioning and scaling the elytra as ellipsoid spheres relative to the body height, checking the bottom doesn't sink too far below the floor, and adjusting body y-position to compensate.

I'm placing the pronotum and head geometry pieces, calculating centres and dimensions so each segment slightly overlaps the previous one without visible gaps.

I'm positioning the compound eyes on the head sides, then working out mandible curvature by chaining several path points that sweep outward from the base and curve inward toward the tips.

Setting up jaw chain joint names...

Next I'm sweeping the mandible shape along the jaw chain with a tapered radius, then figuring out where to place an inward-pointing tooth spike partway along that path.

I'm placing two small mandible teeth near the midpoints of each jaw, then setting default rounded caps for the mandible tips. For the antennae, I'm sketching a short elbowed catmull path from the head's base up to a thin forward-angled tip, which I'll sweep with a narrow radius.

For the club tip, I'm flattening a sphere at the antenna's end and fanning three small flattened ellipsoids around it to suggest lamellae, colored dark. Then I'm defining a head joint parented to the body at a fixed offset with no explicit aim so it inherits the body's upward orientation, and I'm sketching out the leg joint chain naming scheme—coxa, femur, tibia, tarsus—matching four points per leg for three spans plus a tip.

Now I'm placing the hip positions for front, middle, and hind legs along the thorax, setting foot target positions splayed outward and forward/backward per pair, and checking that segment lengths (totaling about 0.037) comfortably exceed the hip-to-foot distances so the legs can bend naturally with inward hints. I'm also sizing the leg sweep radius and considering adding claw spikes at the tarsus tips pointing downward.

Actually, I decide to skip the claws since they'd sink into the floor, and instead keep the foot tip simple with its small sweep radius resting just above the ground. For the elytra surface, I'm planning to use a grain texture running along the long axis to give it a realistic streaked look.

A thin dark seam box will mark the division between the elytra halves, visible along the top ridge. I'm skipping extra ridges and hindwings for budget reasons, but I'll add an abdomen ellipsoid tucked under the back of the elytra for a more complete underside.

Now I'm placing the head box forward of the pronotum with a small neck sphere filling the gap between them, then positioning the mandible bases at the front corners of the head so they emerge naturally. I'm figuring out eye placement on the head sides, using a scaled sphere to give the compound eyes an oval, slightly bulging shape with a shiny look.

Setting up imports from the builder library and starting the main build function...

Defining the elytra paint texture, joint hierarchy for body and head, then placing mirrored elytra parts as scaled spheres with a seam box down the middle.

I'm checking the seam ridge alignment against the elytra curvature, then roughing in the pronotum, abdomen, and head boxes with their own colors and bone attachments.

Now I'm positioning the eyes as small scaled spheres on the head, and defining curved mandible paths with catmull splines so I can build jaw chains with unique bone names per side.

Setting up the jaw joint names, sweeping the mandible tube from base to tip radius, and adding a small inward-facing spike tooth partway along the mandible using the chain's frame at a given parameter.

Now I'm building the antennae as catmull-rom chains rising from the head, naming the joint segments, sweeping thin tubes along them, and capping each with three overlapping flattened spheres to approximate the antenna club, positioning them so the base sits inside the head geometry near the top-front.

Then I'm defining each leg as a chain generated by a limb function from hip to foot with bend directions, naming the coxa/femur/tibia/tarsus joints, sweeping a tube along the chain, and adding a small rigid sphere bulb at the knee joint for visual bulk.

I'm checking the front/mid/hind leg hip and foot coordinates to make sure each leg's reach stays within the three-segment limb length limit, adjusting the front foot's x position slightly to keep it under the max reach, and confirming the hip joints sit comfortably under the elytra and body joint.

I'm skipping decorative details like claws, elytra spots, and pronotum ridges for simplicity. I'm deciding to introduce a scale constant of 0.4 and a helper function that multiplies coordinate arrays and sizes by that factor, so the design-unit numbers I already worked out get converted to realistic dimensions — bringing the total length to roughly 7.6 cm with mandibles around 2.5 cm, which is plausible for a male stag beetle.

I'm checking the small details like foot positions sinking slightly into the floor and the elytra height working out to about 1 cm, which lines up with real proportions. Now I'm setting up the scaling helper constants in code.

Writing beetle geometry code...

I'm checking that nothing hangs below the floor plane — the elytra bottom clears fine, but I need the feet to actually touch down. I'm adjusting the foot sphere's y-position and radius so its bottom sits exactly at zero, keeping the lowest contact points grounded.

Now I'm placing the remaining body parts — the seam box, pronotum sphere with its scale, and the abdomen and neck shapes — assigning each a bone, position, and scale using the design-to-meter conversion consistently.

Then I'm building the head and face: the head box, its front plate, the mirrored eye spheres, and the mandible chains with their joint points and naming convention, assigning the jaw role to the mandible chains for the rigger.

Now I'm sweeping the mandible with a tapering radius, confirming the catmull spline has four spans, then adding teeth as spikes positioned along the jaw chain with directions angled toward the inner side, followed by setting up the antenna chain points and naming its joints.

Next I'm sweeping the antenna with a tapering radius, then building a three-lobed club at the tip using small ellipsoid scales positioned around the end point, before moving on to defining the three leg pairs (fore, mid, hind) with hip and foot coordinates and building each limb's chain points with tapering radii.

Each leg chain is named per side and segment (coxa, femur, tibia, tarsus), swept with a tapering leg color, and I'm adding a knee bulb sphere at the second joint to bulk up that area. I'm double-checking that joint indexing lines up correctly with the chain points so the knee bulb lands on the right segment.

I'll skip claws since the tip point sits too low and would sink below the floor — not worth the visual risk. I'm verifying the mirror helper signature and build setup are correct, making sure the pronotum doesn't overlap the neck/head, and confirming the model faces +Z with the head oriented forward before writing out the final concise code with comments.
